title: What is known about 1RB0RA_0RC0LE_0LD1RA_1LB0RF_0LD1LC_1RD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_0RC0LE_0LD1RA_1LB0RF_0LD1LC_1RD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The two basic counter increments (lowest digit 0, and lowest digits 1 then 0) are proved in Lean for all block lengths (kernel). The general increment rule matches all 2,282 clean increments of the first 3·107 steps, and the C simulator runs 2·1011 steps without a halt. Carries into the higher separators, the reservoir refills and the 1100 region are not yet rules.

One counter, two starts (21 November): this machine is the table of 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA--- started in state D, proved in Lean, and that folder’s exact block macro machine reproduces its run; the reset map and the tail operators found there hold here too, so it is open for the same reason.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Increments for all block lengths
claims.text: From L 1 0 0 (1010)^(n+2) 0 0 (1010)^(m+2) 10 C> 0^∞ the lowest digit becomes 1, the lowest block gains four 10s and the reservoir loses two, in 24m + 12n + 122 steps (inc_d0); with lowest digits 1, 0 (L 1 0 0 (1010)^(a+2) 1 (1010)^(n+2) 0 0 …) both digits flip and both blocks gain two 10s, in 12a + 24m + 12n + 152 steps (inc_d1). half_sweep is the first of the two bounces.

claims.title: The twin's table, started in D
claims.text: This machine is the table of 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA--- in a mirror with the states renamed: it halts from blank tape if and only if that table halts from blank tape started in state D, if and only if that table halts from the record it reaches after 157 steps (twin_halts_iff, twin_reach157, twin_halts_iff_record).

claims.title: Crossing rules of its macro machine
claims.text: The crossing rules that the twin's block macro machine uses in this machine's first 300,000 records (387 shared with the twin's own run in its Rules.lean, 231 more), each for every value of its parameter and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The reset map, for the head of the tape
claims.text: This machine halts if and only if the table of 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA--- halts started in state D (twin_halts_iff); that run is at Reset 52 T0twin after 14,638 steps (reach_twin). From every reset with X ≥ 36 the run reaches the reset with X′ = ⌊3X/2⌋ + 1 (X even) or + 3 (X odd) for every tail whose carries come back with the listed signatures (reset_map); if every phase's carries come back, this machine never halts (never_halts_twin).

claims.title: No halt in the first 2·10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tmrun runs 2·1011 steps without a halt; the tape is then 391,889 cells wide. The shared cycle accelerator finds no cycle rules for this machine.

claims.title: No halt in the first 7.04·10<sup>12</sup> steps (accelerated run, blocks of 4)
claims.text: The run-length simulator tools/c/rleaccel.cpp (blocks of 4 cells, runs of a block crossed in one step, and cycle jumps, each used only after its one-cycle rule has been proved symbolically for all lengths above the minimums it needs; tested cell for cell against direct runs) runs 41,400,000 macro steps from blank tape without a halt, in 10 seconds. That is more than 7.04·1012 machine steps. It found no rule that repeats forever, so it does not decide the machine.

claims.title: The increment rule, checked
claims.text: Low 1-digits become 0, the next 0 becomes 1, its block and the lowest block gain two 10s each, the reservoir loses two. A direct simulation of 3·107 steps finds 2,282 increments that match and none that disagree; 141 carries run into higher separators and 17 reservoir refills fall outside the rule.

claims.title: A second region of 1100s
claims.text: Beyond the counter the machine builds runs of 1100 at the right end (half the tape at step 2·109) and later turns them back into reservoir 10s. Higher separators such as 1101, 0101, 000 appear between long blocks.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when C or E reads a 0 that has a 1 on its left and (10)^k 1 1 on its right. The increments never do this; the refills, long carries and the 1100 region are not closed rules yet. The reset map is proved for the head of the tape (reset_map), so a halt can only happen inside a carry into the tail.

claims.title: An exact macro machine
claims.text: The twin's block macro machine reproduces this run from step 157: same step count, head cell and blocks at all 15,228 records up to step 299,972,981. Its run finds no halt in 300,000 records (1.20·10<sup>11</sup> steps).

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.14×10<sup>134</sup> steps (region-memo accelerator)
claims.text: The region-memo accelerator tools/py/bbtools/regaccel.py ran the mirrored table (so that the counter is at the left end), with blocks of 4 cells, from blank tape for 602 seconds and reached step 3.14×10134 without a halt. It keeps the tape run-length coded and, for each stretch of tape from the left end, a macro (the run until the head first leaves that stretch) computed by a symbolic run of the machine with the long runs as variables; a macro is used only when the linear inequalities its symbolic run assumed hold, otherwise the stretch is run again by the same recursion. So the run is exact, step count included. Check: 8 configurations of this run (every time the head faced blank tape on the right, up to 2×109 steps) agree cell for cell with a direct run (tools/py/regcheck.py). This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: The reset map on the whole run
claims.text: Seen in the mirror, a countdown block X is used up and the next block becomes the countdown; the next reset has X′ = ⌊3X/2⌋ + 1 (X even) or ⌊3X/2⌋ + 3 (X odd): 7, 13, 22, 34, 52, 79, …, 24271 at every one of the 19 transitions of the first 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps; 33 in this machine’s macro run (2·10<sup>7</sup> records, 2.5·10<sup>14</sup> steps, no halt) and 34 in the twin’s (to 3.4·10<sup>14</sup> steps).

claims.title: What the tail sees
claims.text: The rest of the counter (the tail) is acted on by four operators fixed by the parity of the growing block: E0, E1 alternating inside each phase (2,965 of 2,965 increments of the first 6,000 records) and E1 O0 O1 or E1 at a reset (13 of 14 resets). Whether the machine halts is whether this word of operators, spelled out by the 3/2 orbit, ever drives the tail into the halting pattern.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

check: holdouts/1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA---/lean/check.sh      # the twin bridge and crossing rules

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. This machine counts in binary on its tape, writing each digit as a single cell between long runs of 10, and pays for every count with cells from a reservoir. It has run 2·1011 steps without stopping.

facts.text: No halt in the run-length accelerator (proved cycle jumps, blocks of 4).
No halt in the C simulator.
The basic increments, proved for all block lengths.
Increments checked against the rule, none off.
The reset map of its twin's table, proved in Lean for the head of the tape; only the carries into the tail are assumed.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.507).
After 109 steps the tape spans 54,987 cells (20 left of the start, 40,988 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The same counter as its twin
html: This table, read in a mirror with its states renamed, is the table of the holdout 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA---. So this run is that table’s run from blank tape started in state D, proved in Lean (kernel, twin_halts_iff in that folder’s lean/Twin29537.lean). Seen in the mirror, the tape at each left record is a countdown block followed by a binary counter on blocks of 10s, exactly as there, and that folder’s block macro machine reproduces this run record for record (15,228 records, to step 299,972,981). Its 231 crossing rules beyond the twin’s own are proved in Lean for every block size (kernel).

The reset map, exactly. When the countdown runs out, the long block X after it becomes the next countdown, and the next reset has X′ = ⌊3X/2⌋ + 1 (X even) or ⌊3X/2⌋ + 3 (X odd). Here X runs 7, 13, 22, 34, 52, 79, 121, 184, 277, 418, 628, 943, 1417, 2128, 3193, 4792, 7189, 10786, 16180, 24271 in the first 3·109 steps, every step by the rule; 33 in this machine’s macro run (2·107 records, 2.5·1014 steps, no halt) and 34 in the twin’s (to 3.4·1014 steps). The twin is another orbit of the same map.

At the records in the middle of a phase the tape is B>0 (10)^D0 0 0 (10)^Y x T: the countdown D0, the growing block Y with its cell x, and the tail T, everything further on. From one such record to the next (one increment) the tail changes in a way that depends only on whether Y is even and on x — not on the countdown, and not on the size of Y. So there are just four things that can happen to a tail:

operatorblock before the tailwhat it does to the tail’s cells
E0Y even, x = 0lengthens the tail’s first block by one 10, nothing else
E1Y odd, x = 1a carry: a few cells change, sometimes hundreds of cells deep
O0, O1Y odd, x = 0 / Y even, x = 1another carry (the two give the same cells)

Checked on direct runs (py/tail_ops.py in the folder of 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA---): inside every phase Y + x is even, so the tail goes E0, E1, E0, E1, … (2,965 of 2,965 increments in the first 6,000 records here, 1,467 of 1,467 in the twin; 13 of 14 resets here (the first, at X = 7, applies E1 O0), 13 of 13 in the twin); a reset applies E1 O0 O1 when X is even and E1 when X is odd. So the whole future of the tail is one fixed word of operators, spelled out by the orbit of the 3/2 map. Whether the machine halts is the question whether that word ever drives the tail into the halting pattern. The operators do not commute, so the tail is not simply a function of how many increments have happened; this is the Collatz-like core of the problem. All of this is heuristic: checked, not proved.

It also explains why run-length engines stall: the carries leave the tail as a mass of short blocks of different lengths (about 150 to 190 blocks at 3·109 steps), with no long runs to compress beyond the first few blocks.

The reset map, in Lean. Started in state D, the twin's table is at the reset 0^inf 1 B>1 0 (10)^52 T after 14,638 steps (reach_twin), and from every reset with X ≥ 36 the head of the tape follows X → ⌊3X/2⌋ + 1 or + 3 exactly, whatever the tail holds, as long as each carry into the tail comes back (reset_map, never_halts_twin in the twin's folder). So this machine, too, can halt only inside such a carry.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: Almost the whole tape is runs of the two-cell word 10 (accent colour). Between two runs there is a single extra cell, and that cell is a digit: …1 0 [0] 1 0… is a 0 and …1 0 [1] 1 0… is a 1 (orange). At the right end, after the lowest digit and its run, come a marker 0 0 and a reservoir of 10s (grey); the head is on the blank cell after it.

sections.heading: One increment
html: The head bounces twice between the right end and the low digits. The first bounce turns the marker 0 0 into 1 10 1; the second turns it back and adds one to the binary number read from the digits: the lowest 1s become 0, the next 0 becomes 1. The run after the digit where the carry stopped, and the lowest run, each get two more 10s; the reservoir gives up two.

sections.heading: A counter that pays for itself
html: The number stored in the digits goes up by one per increment, and the runs grow with it: run j gains two 10s every 2j increments, so the tape gets longer and each increment takes longer. The reservoir runs out regularly; the machine then refills it. Further right it also builds a second kind of region, made of the four-cell word 1100: at step 2·109 about half the tape is 1100s, and these are turned back into reservoir 10s later. High in the counter the separators are not always single cells (1101, 0101, 000 appear), a second layer of structure that the rules above do not cover.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is F reading 1. Tracing back through D, the machine halts exactly when C or E stands on a 0 with a 1 on its left and (1 0)k 1 1 on its right: on this tape, inside a run of 10s that ends in a 1-digit. If the run ends in a 0-digit instead, the machine escapes into state B. The proved increments never do this; whether a refill, a long carry or the 1100 region ever does is the open part.

sections.heading: What is proved
html:
• Kernel: the increments half_sweep, inc_d0, inc_d1 for all run lengths (lean/Rules.lean); no halt in 10,000 steps.
  • native_decide: no halt in 107 steps.
  • Trusted computation: no halt in 2·1011 steps; the increment rule matches 2,282 increments.
  • Open: whether it ever halts.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LF_0LC0RE_0RA1LD_1LB0LD_0RA1RC_1LA---: rename A→D, B→B, C→C, D→A, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror

family: binary counter with growing digit blocks and a reservoir
summary: A binary counter written in runs of 10s with one-cell digits; each increment spends two 10s of a reservoir at the right end and lengthens the blocks next to the carry; the basic increments are proved in Lean. Accelerated run: no halt in 7.04e12 steps.
